   - Write Lambda architecture sample
   - Write documentation

3. **U2: Sqoop batch sample**
   - Design Sqoop batch job wrapper
   - Implement JDBC to HDFS job
   - Implement HDFS to JDBC job
   - Write documentation

4. **U3: Gradle script updates**
   - Update gradle doc generation
   - Remove pushGeneratedDocs task
   - Remove link rewriting code

5. **U4: Storm examples comparison doc**
   - Research existing Storm examples in XD
   - Write comparison document

6. **U5: Spark Streaming examples comparison doc**
   - Research existing Spark Streaming examples in XD
   - Write comparison document

7. **U6: Smart Grid demo port**
   - Locate original Smart Grid demo
   - Port to XD samples repo
   - Update configuration and dependencies
   - Test and document

8. **U7: JDBC to HDFS example**
   - Create example configuration
   - Write sample data and scripts
   - Write documentation

9. **U8: File sink naming flexibility**
   - Design --nameExpression option
   - Implement option parsing
   - Wire up to filename generator
   - Write tests
   - Update documentation

10. **Integration Testing**
    - Test all samples in XD environment
    - Verify documentation builds correctly

11. **Final Review**
    - Code review
    - Documentation review

- U1 Kafka pipeline: 24 hours (it's complex with multiple use cases)
- U2 Sqoop batch: 16 hours
- U3 Gradle updates: 4 hours
- U4 Storm comparison: 6 hours
- U5 Spark Streaming comparison: 6 hours
- U6 Smart Grid port: 16 hours
- U7 JDBC to HDFS: 8 hours
- U8 File sink naming: 12 hours
- Integration testing: 8 hours
- Final review: 4 hours

Total: 4 + 24 + 16 + 4 + 6 + 6 + 16 + 8 + 12 + 8 + 4 = 108 hours

technical_and_design_decisions: Target platform is Spring XD running on a JDK 17+ runtime as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
Reuse the existing Spring XD module/spi APIs (source, sink, processor, job) rather than introduce new abstractions, to keep code consistent with the rest of the samples repo.

Kafka integration (U1) will be built on top of the existing Kafka source/sink modules already shipped in Spring XD; the work focuses on wiring up demonstrative stream/batch definitions, not implementing a new Kafka client from scratch.

Sqoop integration (U2) will be packaged as an XD batch job (spark/hadoop backed) that shells out to the Sqoop CLI or invokes Sqoop's Java API, rather than re-implementing JDBC-to-HDFS data movement natively.

The Smart Grid demo (U6) will be ported as a self-contained XD sample module set (stream definitions + supporting classes) reproducing the s1-2014 functionality, not as a separate standalone Spring Boot app.
Documentation will be authored in Asciidoctor to match the existing Spring XD samples repo convention.

For U8, the new --nameExpression option will be implemented as a sibling to the existing --name and --suffix options on the file sink module, evaluated through SpEL, and the deprecated link-rewriting logic (U3) will be removed entirely rather than left as dead code.
Storm (U4) and Spark Streaming (U5) comparison documents will be static reference tables/matrices (no executable code) summarizing API, semantics, and how each maps to XD constructs.
assumptions: The Spring XD samples repository is already cloned and builds successfully before starting development.
A working Kafka cluster (or embedded Kafka) and an HDFS-compatible filesystem are available in the developer's local environment for integration verification.
The original Smart Grid demo (s1-2014) source artifacts are accessible in the internal repository or can be reconstructed from the published demo description.
Sqoop 1.x is installed and reachable; JDBC drivers for the source/target databases are available.
All effort estimates cover coding, local testing, and writing accompanying documentation; no formal QA, design review meetings, or end-to-end cluster deployment are included.
The file-sink module in the targeted Spring XD version already exposes a filename-generator-expression attribute that simply needs to be made user-configurable through a new command-line option.
One developer performs all activities (no coordination overhead), working normal productive hours.
Existing XD integration tests for file sink are sufficient and only need minor extension for the new --nameExpression option.

activities.activity_description: Clone/checkout the Spring XD samples repository, verify the build with Gradle, configure IDE, and ensure all required modules (Kafka, Sqoop, Storm, Spark Streaming, file sink) build and resolve dependencies on JDK 17+.

Design and implement an XD stream definition that uses Kafka as the message bus, including: (a) a log-aggregation pipeline, (b) a Lambda-architecture pipeline showing how to avoid code duplication and tight coupling of business logic, and (c) a reliable reprocessing demo. Implement supporting source/sink/processor code, sample data, and Asciidoctor documentation.

Build an XD batch job sample that uses Sqoop to move data: (a) JDBC to HDFS and (b) HDFS to JDBC. Wire Sqoop invocation into the XD job lifecycle, supply sample JDBC sources, and write Asciidoctor documentation explaining setup and execution.

Modify the Gradle build script to update the documentation generation task, remove the obsolete pushGeneratedDocs task, and remove the no-longer-needed link-rewriting logic. Verify that the Asciidoctor documentation still builds cleanly.

Review the existing Storm-based stream definitions in Spring XD and produce a comparison/reference document that makes it easy for a field engineer to relate XD constructs to their Storm implementation counterparts (topology, spout, bolt mappings, parallelism, reliability).

activities.activity_name: U5 - Spark Streaming examples comparison document
activities.activity_description: Review the existing Spark Streaming stream definitions in Spring XD and produce a comparison/reference document that maps XD constructs (source, sink, processor, taps) to Spark Streaming concepts (DStream, receiver, output operation, sliding window) for field engineers.

Port the s1-2014 Smart Grid demo into the Spring XD samples repository as an XD-native sample: re-create the stream/batch definitions, supporting domain classes, simulated sensor data, dashboards/output sinks, and README/Asciidoctor walkthrough so it runs end-to-end on XD.

activities.activity_name: U7 - JDBC to HDFS data movement example
activities.activity_description: Create a small, focused example (separate from the broader Sqoop sample in U2) that demonstrates JDBC-to-HDFS data movement using XD's existing JDBC source and HDFS sink modules, including a sample schema, sample records, and a short Asciidoctor how-to.

Extend the XD file sink module to accept a new --nameExpression command-line option that gives full SpEL control over the underlying filename-generator-expression attribute. Implement option parsing, SpEL evaluation, integration with the existing filename generator, extend unit/integration tests, and update reference documentation for the file sink.

Run all new and modified samples (Kafka pipeline, Sqoop batch, Smart Grid demo, JDBC-to-HDFS, file-sink with --nameExpression) end-to-end against a local XD single-node runtime; verify the rebuilt documentation site renders correctly and the cleaned-up Gradle build passes.

Self-review of all code changes, Asciidoctor documentation, comparison documents, and the cleaned-up Gradle build. Fix any issues found during review and ensure consistent formatting, naming, and sample structure across the increment.
